solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Significant political party face Republican expert

parts.note: CON is the short form of Conservative, the UK political party
to face something is to side, as a building's side faces the street
an able person is skilled or expert

explanation.surface: A notable figure: a party man who also looks the part of a Republican specialist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'face' is taken as a noun meaning a surface, SIDE.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe something large or important in amount or degree; a direct synonym.

clue.text: A living thing's heart perhaps is beginning to move

parts.note: the heart is an example of a bodily organ, hence 'perhaps'

indicators.note: the beginning of the word move gives its opening letter only

explanation.surface: Seems to describe a creature whose heart is just starting to beat.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's after 'A living thing' stands for 'is' and links definition to wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Any individual plant, animal or microbe is a life form; this is the biological term for one.

clue.text: Last ones in hike off-road stumble upon idyllic place

indicators.note: the last letters in the four following words are taken, one from each

explanation.surface: Walkers leaving the track happen upon a perfect spot in the countryside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Last ones in' looks like the stragglers on a hike, but signals final letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The biblical garden of paradise is used for any place of perfect peace and beauty.

clue.text: English Queen, the fourth to back European city

indicators.note: to back means to run backwards, so the letters of the queen and numeral are read in reverse

parts.note: Anne was Queen of England (and then Great Britain) from 1702
IV is four in Roman numerals, as in a regnal title

explanation.surface: Suggests a royal list where a fourth monarch supports a European capital.
explanation.definitionFit: The Austrian capital on the Danube is a major city of central Europe.

clue.text: He's paid for risky feats, double maybe

definitions.meaning: a professional who performs dangerous film action for pay
a body double who stands in for an actor in perilous scenes

explanation.surface: Describes a daredevil professional, and hints he might be someone's lookalike.
explanation.walkthrough: Both halves describe the same film professional, one by his job, one by his role as stand-in.
explanation.definitionFit: Film crews hire such performers for falls and crashes, and they often impersonate the star on screen.

clue.text: Showing heart repeatedly, work pal's spoken

indicators.note: the heart of each of two words is shown in turn, so the middle letters of both are taken

explanation.surface: Seems to describe a colleague who keeps declaring his feelings out loud.
explanation.walkthrough: The middle of 'work' is OR and the middle two of 'pal's' are AL.
explanation.definitionFit: Something oral is delivered by mouth rather than written, as in an oral exam.

clue.text: Regular characters in local, flushed, had a row

indicators.note: regular here means every other letter of the word local, the second and fourth

parts.note: a flushed face is red

explanation.surface: A red-faced drinker in the pub had an argument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'had a row' suggests a quarrel, but here it means rowing a boat.
explanation.definitionFit: A boat that has been oared was propelled with oars; to row is to work the oars.

clue.text: Popular one in academic period is temporary

parts.note: something in fashion or popular is said to be in

indicators.note: in says the letter for one sits inside the word for an academic period

parts.note: a school or university term
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A popular student's success during one term is only short-lived.
explanation.definitionFit: An interim arrangement holds only until a permanent one is made, so it is provisional.

clue.text: Clearing bombs from pits, visible upset

parts.note: mines are pits dug for coal or ore
weeping shows distress openly, so it is upset made visible

explanation.surface: A tearful scene as explosives are cleared from quarries.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' looks like an anagram signal, but 'visible upset' is simply crying.
explanation.definitionFit: Naval sweeping removes explosive sea mines, the task of the minesweeper vessel.

clue.text: Quiet woman on river

parts.note: sh is the call for silence
Ann is a woman's name

explanation.surface: A peaceful lady sitting by a river.
explanation.walkthrough: The Shannon is the longest river in Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: Ireland's longest river flows from County Cavan to the Atlantic near Limerick.

clue.text: Only altered new fabric

indicators.note: altered means the letters of the word only are changed into a new order

explanation.surface: Only an altered garment is made of new material.
explanation.definitionFit: Nylon is a synthetic polymer woven into cloth for stockings and sportswear.

clue.text: Welshman tracks remote maiden where cows are milked?

parts.note: Dai is a typical Welsh man's name, short for David
RY is short for railway, a set of tracks
far means distant or remote
M stands for maiden, an over in cricket with no runs scored

explanation.surface: A Welshman follows tracks to a lonely spot where cattle are milked.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks a definition by example: milking is one thing done there.
explanation.definitionFit: A farm that keeps cattle for milk and milk products is where milking takes place.

clue.text: Mad Cathy has drunk gin, guiding an aquatic vessel

indicators.note: mad says the letters of the name Cathy go wild and rearrange
drunk says the letters of the word gin are scrambled like a tipsy reveller

explanation.surface: Wild Cathy downs some gin while steering a boat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mad' shuffles CATHY into YACHT and 'drunk' shuffles GIN into ING; 'has' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Sailing a pleasure boat for sport or leisure is the activity of steering one on the water.

clue.text: Father's dance step

definitions.meaning: a dad's, possessive of the informal word for father
the French word for a step in ballet

explanation.surface: Seems to describe Dad's move on the dance floor.
explanation.definitionFit: The ballet term for a step is French, and the same letters spell the possessive of a short word for dad.

clue.text: Training copper who tells lies: strange

parts.note: PE is physical education, a school's fitness training
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
someone who tells lies is a liar

explanation.surface: A policeman in training who lies is an odd one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'copper' looks like a policeman but gives the chemical symbol.
explanation.definitionFit: Peculiar and strange are synonyms meaning odd or unusual.

clue.text: Pack run in the morning

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for run
a.m. marks a time before noon

explanation.surface: A group goes for a jog before noon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pack' looks like a group of runners but is a verb, to cram.
explanation.definitionFit: To cram or press tightly is to force something in, as one does stuffing a case.

clue.text: Church function includes mostly pleasant historical record

indicators.note: includes means the word for function holds the next piece inside it

parts.note: a role is a function or job

indicators.note: mostly means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: nice means pleasant

explanation.surface: A church service with a pleasant element, written into the annals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'function' here means a part played, not a social event; 'mostly' drops the last letter of the word for pleasant.
explanation.definitionFit: A chronicle is an account of events set down in the order they happened.

clue.text: Scam that's employed in court

definitions.meaning: the strung bat used on a tennis or squash court

explanation.surface: Suggests a fraud being used in a court of law.
explanation.walkthrough: 'court' suggests law, but it is a tennis court.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a dishonest scheme and the strung bat used in tennis.

clue.text: Piece of sculpture, disturbed by king, broke into pieces

indicators.note: disturbed by means the sculpture is broken into by the king's letter

parts.note: a bust is a sculpture of head and shoulders
R is short for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: A statue knocked by a king shattered.
explanation.definitionFit: To burst is to break apart suddenly and violently, as a balloon or pipe does.

clue.text: Engrossed artist emptied paint

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, a crossword artist

indicators.note: emptied means the inside letters of the word paint are removed, leaving its ends

explanation.surface: An absorbed painter has used up all the paint.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone rapt is so absorbed that they notice nothing else.

clue.text: Headwear around flat spoiled access for pet

indicators.note: around means the hat goes about the next letters

parts.note: a cap is a hat

indicators.note: spoiled means the letters of the word flat are damaged and reordered

explanation.surface: A hat left around a messed-up flat, and a way in for the cat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flat' looks like a home, but is just anagram fodder; 'spoiled' gives TFLA.
explanation.definitionFit: A small hinged door fitted in a house door lets a cat come and go.

clue.text: Printing error in naughty postcard

indicators.note: in says the letters are found inside the phrase naughty postcard

explanation.surface: A misprint on a saucy seaside postcard.
explanation.walkthrough: Naughty postcards are a British seaside tradition of cheeky cartoons.
explanation.definitionFit: A slip in typing or typesetting is a misprint.

clue.text: Divorcee confines energy outlay

parts.note: an ex is a former spouse
to pen is to confine, so pens means confines
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A former spouse limits how much power is spent.
explanation.definitionFit: Money laid out on something is spending, a cost incurred.

clue.text: Man on board eating right seafood

indicators.note: eating means the chess piece swallows the letter for right

parts.note: a pawn is a chess man on the board

explanation.surface: A passenger aboard ship tucks into shellfish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Man on board' suggests a ship's passenger, but means a chess piece.
explanation.definitionFit: This shellfish is a small crustacean eaten as seafood.
